answers.answer: Open Pipelines and choose New pipeline, type a name in Name and choose Make pipeline. Choose Add a step at the end, pick Send message under Chat and write the line in Message. Add Grant currency under Economy the same way and set Amount, then choose Save above the steps and wait for 'Pipeline saved.' To check it, leave How to run at Dry run and choose Test run. Each step card shows Done, Failed or Did not run, and Clear test run takes the results off.

You need the Moderator role or a higher one to make, change or try a pipeline. A step that uses OBS, the music player, VTube Studio or Discord needs that connection set up before a live run. Both are stated under Before you start.
answers.quote: A Moderator or a higher role can make and change pipelines, and only those roles can try one from the editor, in a dry run or a live run.

answers.answer: After Test run, each step card shows its result, and the header of the steps card shows a run count. After Run now, a notice lists the steps that ran for real. In Runs, the labels Test run and Live run tell editor runs apart from real starts. A dry run's Done on Send message only means the line would have gone out.
answers.quote: Each step card now shows its result: Done, Failed or Did not run.

answers.answer: Viewers cannot trigger the pipeline until a command, chat trigger, timer or event response points to it, so the moderator can test it first. A dry run sends no chat and changes no balance: Send message and Grant currency are only recorded as Done. To see the line in chat and the balance change, the moderator uses Run live. That run starts as the moderator, so the currency goes to the moderator's own balance. After that, the moderator connects the pipeline to a command on the Commands page.
answers.quote: It starts as you, so Grant currency adds to your own balance, and a ban or timeout step acts on a real viewer.

answers.answer: I reread once: the editor resets to Dry run on each open, which is stated only after the live-run steps. That costs one extra click when someone expects Run live to still be selected. Nothing blocked a step.
answers.quote: The editor goes back to Dry run each time you open it.

answers.answer: When read aloud, 'at the bottom' does not say which screen; the context implies the pipeline editor, so it costs a moment of looking. The text Test run is used for both the run button and the label in Runs, but the page says so, so it is not an obstacle.
answers.quote: Delete pipeline at the bottom asks first and names each command, trigger, timer or event response that would stop running anything.
